question: A man travels 120 km at 40 km/h and returns the same distance at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** traveled is the same for both parts of a journey, the **Average Speed** is calculated using the harmonic mean formula: 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Here, x = 40 km/h and y = 60 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 40 × 60) ÷ (40 + 60)

Average Speed = 4800 ÷ 100 = 48 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance for each trip = 120 km

Speed during onward journey (S₁) = 40 km/h

Speed during return journey (S₂) = 60 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d884251922cfa1df1cda67a225484bf68b4b9cb02c78ead40a7a35d4b86a314.png] 

**Formula:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Time taken for onward journey (T₁) = Distance ÷ S₁ = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey (T₂) = Distance ÷ S₂ = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 120 = 240 km

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 2 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a person travels at speed S₁ and S₂ for equal time intervals, the Average Speed is the arithmetic mean: (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, relative speed is (S₁ + S₂). In the **same direction**, it is |S₁ − S₂|.</p
